szoveg_eredeti:
Loizos G. Loizou, Head of Cyprus International Action Plan for Children with Cancer at ELPIDA Foundation for Children with Cancer, shared on LinkedIn:

Breast Cancer and Artificial Intelligence: New hopes for saving lives?

Mammography saves lives, but some cancers escape diagnosis.

At the same time, evaluating millions of mammograms requires significant time from specialized doctors.

In Britain, the major clinical study EDITH has begun, aiming to involve 660,000 women to evaluate the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in mammography screening.

AI will help identify suspicious lesions without removing the need for a specialist doctor.

The Swedish study MASAI showed that, with the help of AI:

AI can contribute to early diagnosis and more effective utilization of health services.

However, it needs to be proven that the benefits are achieved without increasing unnecessary tests and overdiagnosis.

Artificial Intelligence does not replace the doctor.

However, it can become a valuable partner for better prevention and early diagnosis.

NHS Launches World’s Largest Breast Cancer Screening Trial Involving 660,000 Participants
